clue.text: Nancy's very amorous advance gives offence

parts.note: Nancy is a French city, so its word for 'very' is the French très
to make a pass is to make a romantic approach

explanation.surface: A woman named Nancy rebuffs an over-eager admirer whose advances have upset her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a woman's name but is the city in north-east France, so her 'very' is in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespass is a sin or wrongdoing, as in the Lord's Prayer's 'forgive us our trespasses'.

clue.text: Gradient Newton proved

parts.note: a rise is an upward slope
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: A physicist establishes a slope; Isaac Newton demonstrated something about inclines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proved' sounds like demonstrated, but it is the baker's sense: dough that has proved has swollen.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread dough left to prove has risen, so the baking term matches the past participle.

clue.text: US public servants observed alien eating some people

parts.note: to observe can mean to remark or state

indicators.note: something that eats takes food inside it, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: E.T. is the film's extraterrestrial
part of a group of men

explanation.surface: American officials watched an extraterrestrial devour a few humans.
explanation.walkthrough: The alien goes round the people, and the whole sits after the word for observed.
explanation.definitionFit: The State Department is the US government ministry handling foreign affairs, staffed by public servants.

clue.text: Spread out, running laps around green

indicators.note: around puts one piece on both sides of another
running letters are in motion and get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
green, as in inexperienced or unripe, is raw

explanation.surface: An athlete sprawls on the grass after doing circuits of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Asprawl is a literary adjective for lying with limbs stretched out, sprawling.

clue.text: Godparent quietly breaks child's soldiers

indicators.note: something that breaks into another gets inside it

parts.note: a son is a child; the possessive gives the s
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
OR is Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: At a christening, the godparent tiptoes in and smashes the child's toy soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor at a baptism is the godparent who makes promises on the child's behalf.

clue.text: Two scams a realtor's offering?

parts.note: first of the two: a con is a swindle
second of the two: a do is a swindle

explanation.surface: A cynic suggests what an estate agent sells is a double swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: Both scam words are needed side by side; realtor is the American for estate agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A condo, short for condominium, is an American apartment that an estate agent would sell.

clue.text: Rogue wed Angolan clerk for sex

indicators.note: a rogue element is out of order, so these letters run wild

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scoundrel married an office worker from Angola for the obvious reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like a noun naming the bridegroom, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal knowledge is the old legal and biblical euphemism for sexual intercourse.

clue.text: Boss less sensitive dealing with termination of workforce

parts.note: more numb
on means about or concerning

indicators.note: a termination is an ending, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hard-hearted boss makes redundancies among the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a callous manager sacking workers; 'less sensitive' is a comparative of numb, a different pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one is an informal term for the person in charge, the top dog.

clue.text: Duck, swan, not decided yet?

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the shape of O
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: At the pond, a birdwatcher can't tell whether that's a duck or a swan.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An open question is one still unresolved, awaiting a decision.

clue.text: Billions, when you shouldn't have enough!

parts.note: b is the abbreviation for billion
as can mean while or when
ta is British slang for thanks, which is what 'you shouldn't have' expresses

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a gift of billions is too much; they already have plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have' is what you say when thanking someone for a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Basta is Italian for 'that will do', used in English as an exclamation meaning stop.

clue.text: Bishop wittering on, forgetting Welsh is incomprehensible

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out of the word

parts.note: to witter on is to talk at length about nothing
W is the abbreviation for Welsh

explanation.surface: A bishop rambles in his sermon and forgets to speak Welsh, leaving the congregation lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Something baffling is puzzling and impossible to understand.

clue.text: Order of Service is one for mass

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
the gramme is a unit of mass

explanation.surface: The leaflet handed out in church is the one for the Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service but is the physics quantity; the leaflet setting out a service is a printed programme.
explanation.definitionFit: An order of service is the printed sheet listing hymns and readings, a church programme.

clue.text: European adjusted Kane's wage for very hard work

parts.note: a Finn is a native of Finland

indicators.note: adjusted things are altered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A European club renegotiated footballer Harry Kane's salary, a gruelling job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a literary work: James Joyce's last novel, notoriously difficult to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce's Finnegans Wake is famously among the hardest novels in English, a very hard book.

clue.text: Moisturiser Nosferatu applied, with nothing to lose?

indicators.note: applied letters are put to new use and set in a new order
nothing is the round letter, and losing it drops it from the name

parts.note: taken as written: the vampire of the 1922 film

explanation.surface: The vampire Nosferatu, who avoids daylight, puts on skin cream anyway, having nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: Nothing is O; drop it from the vampire's name and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftersun is a lotion applied to soothe and moisturise skin after sunbathing.

clue.text: Drink on account, opening two litres of milk

indicators.note: what opens a pair splits it, sitting between them

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for litre, twice

indicators.note: in an across clue, one item on another follows it

parts.note: ac is the abbreviation for account
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone buys drinks on a tab and cracks open two litres of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacteal is the technical adjective meaning relating to or resembling milk.

clue.text: Crease my carpet had

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
a rug is a small carpet
to have a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their carpet has a crease in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation 'my!', which a Briton might say as cor.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrugate is to fold or wrinkle into ridges, making creases.

clue.text: Libertine taking no unearned share of proceeds

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man
to be off something, like drink, is to take none of it

explanation.surface: A womaniser refuses to take any cut from his ill-gotten gains.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is a commission or cut, often illicit, skimmed from profits.

clue.text: Group of five in Narnia? That's wrong

indicators.note: in places one item inside another
a wrong order needs correcting, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: C. S. Lewis's fantasy land
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A pedant objects that the Famous Five never went to Narnia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' is a rock band, the trio fronted by Kurt Cobain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana was the American grunge band of the early 1990s, a musical group.

clue.text: Simple vessel trawler nets capsized

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue the letters run the other way
a net encloses its catch, so the answer is caught within the words

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A fishing boat's nets overturn a little boat at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means natural and without guile, so plain and simple.

clue.text: Language models love (needless) brackets

indicators.note: the words bracket something, holding it inside them

parts.note: the letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A dig at AI chatbots, which are fond of unnecessary parenthetical asides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Language models' reads as one phrase about AI; split it, and the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovene is the South Slavic tongue spoken in Slovenia.

clue.text: Criminal who's too quick touching bottoms up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters climb from bottom to top

parts.note: re means concerning, touching on
the deeps are the lowest depths of the sea

explanation.surface: A drinker downs glasses too fast; 'bottoms up' is the toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottoms up' is a toast; here the phrase splits, with 'up' working alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A speeder is a motorist breaking the speed limit, an offender for going too fast.

clue.text: Your decision left leading rowers completely immersed

parts.note: it's 'up to thee', in old-fashioned form, if the decision is yours
L is the abbreviation for left
the bow oars are the rowers nearest the front of the boat

explanation.surface: A coach leaves it to someone to pick which rower should lead the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to the elbows is an idiom for being deeply involved or busy, as if plunged in.

clue.text: Newspaper Stanley's partner hasn't opened

indicators.note: without its opening, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: Morgan Stanley is an American investment bank

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports that a banker's business partner has yet to open his doors.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley's partner suggests Livingstone or Laurel's Ollie, but it is the bank Morgan Stanley.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a publication that speaks for a party or group, such as a newspaper.

clue.text: Terrible being so upset

indicators.note: upset things are turned over, so in a down clue the letters run upwards

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so

explanation.surface: Someone is dreadfully hurt by what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible being' reads as being very upset; it is a noun phrase, a fearsome creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous giant from folklore, a frightening creature.

clue.text: Kent town goes crazy after good goal

indicators.note: after sets the following pieces behind the first

parts.note: g is the abbreviation for good
to rave is to rant wildly
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: The crowd at a Kent football ground erupts after a fine goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravesend is a town on the Thames estuary in Kent, England.

clue.text: Start course to make your position more secure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tuck in to a course of a meal
second meaning: entrench, as soldiers do

explanation.surface: A student begins a course in order to secure their career.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to start eating heartily and to entrench oneself defensively.

clue.text: Up before court

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone is up in front of the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means upright, standing straight up.

clue.text: Copper turned green as mint, in the end

indicators.note: turned letters are rotated out of their original order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A copper coin has oxidised green, its mint condition eventually lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests the metal turning green with age; it is a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a police rank, and copper is informal for a police officer.
